about: Retained regression cases of the economic-consistency slice (29 October 2026), copied from the saved records by data/local-checks/econ-consistency-2026-10-29/make_consistency_cases.py. Real cases, not SYNTHETIC: our saved brief versions exactly (the published Šefčovič v5 and von der Leyen v1), and of the European Commission publications only the sentences the tests need. reports.title: Halvard Quennel: Interview with Harbour Ledger
reports.excerpt:
Parliament is expected to approve the currency amendment before the summer recess, and the Board would then fix the withdrawal date.
Is there a ceiling on how many old notes a household can swap?
There is, but spending old notes will stay unrestricted until the withdrawal date.
The ceiling applies to exchanges at our branches, not to purchases in shops.
Anyone holding more than the ceiling can pay the surplus into a bank account instead, where it is credited in full.
The new series goes into circulation in 2027, after a closed trial run by our branch staff.
Our stress tests suggest that a household cap on exchanges will not trouble the commercial banks' cash handling.
The ceiling is meant to prevent queues in the final weeks, when most people tend to arrive.
In our latest survey, notes older than ten years made up 41% of those in circulation in 2021 and 33% in 2025.

trade-safeguards.limits: An investigation may end without a measure; a measure's form, size and duration are set later, within the agreement's limits.
trade-safeguards.mechanism: Under WTO rules a member may restrict imports of a product temporarily, by a quota or a higher tariff applied to all sources, if an investigation finds that increased imports cause or threaten serious injury to a domestic industry; injury from other causes must not be attributed to imports. An investigation comes before any measure: protection for domestic producers and higher costs for buyers of the product would follow only if a measure is imposed, and affected exporters may seek compensation or suspend equivalent concessions.

facts.text: The European Commission says the EU's trade deficit with China reached almost €197 billion in the first half of 2026, and that at this rate it could exceed the 2022 record of €397 billion.

Next steps named: a safeguard on hybrids and plug-in hybrids to be initiated soon; identification of further priority sectors using the Import Barometer, which tracks sustained import surges harming EU industry; and a meeting with Chinese counterparts next month.

content.summary: After an informal meeting of EU trade ministers in Dublin, Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said the EU's deficit with China reached almost €197 billion in the first half of 2026 and that rebalancing is the Commission's central workstream, starting with a safeguard on hybrids and plug-in hybrids "to be initiated soon". He said the Commission will table a DiversifyEU package in December and propose ways to make its trade defence tools more effective. On the United States, he said EU exports grew 3.5% in 2025, to €555 billion.

facts.text: Von der Leyen said the EU and China agreed an annual quota of 350 000 hybrid vehicles from China, reducing exports by around 45%, to be implemented through a safeguard.
She said Chinese hybrid electric vehicle exports to the EU had risen from $2.5 billion to $7.5 billion in twelve months.
She said China agreed to cut tariffs on EU products worth almost €4 billion and gave greater predictability on export controls for rare earths and magnets.

She said the EU's trade deficit with China reached €1 billion a day in 2025, and that the Commission will present a DiversifyEU package in December and propose a new instrument to limit access to the Single Market when EU interests are threatened.

She said the Commission's simplification proposals could save over €22 billion of administrative burden a year if all are agreed, and that the Commission will develop a plan for a European Energy Union.
She said energy sanctions on Russia will stay until Russia stops the war.

content.headline: Von der Leyen says China agreed an annual quota of 350 000 hybrid cars for the EU, to be implemented through a safeguard

implications.text: If the quota is applied as described, Chinese hybrid supplies to the EU could fall, which may support EU hybrid producers and could raise what buyers pay.
EU exporters of the products covered by China's tariff cuts could face lower duties, though the speech does not name the products.
Chemicals and machinery, which she named as sectors facing growing concerns, may see trade defence measures if dialogue does not deliver.

missing: The text of the agreement with China.
The contents of the DiversifyEU package and of the new deterrence instrument.
content.summary: Reporting to the European Parliament on the European Council of 15-16 October, Commission President von der Leyen said dialogue with China had produced an annual quota of 350 000 hybrid vehicles from China, which she said reduces those exports by around 45% and will be implemented through a safeguard, after Chinese hybrid exports to the EU rose from $2.5 billion to $7.5 billion in twelve months. She said China agreed to cut tariffs on EU products worth almost €4 billion, announced a DiversifyEU package for December and a new deterrence instrument, and said energy sanctions on Russia will stay until it stops the war.
uncertainties: The quota's legal form, start date and duration are not given; she said only that it will be implemented through a safeguard.
The base against which exports fall by around 45% is not stated.
Which EU products benefit from China's tariff cuts is not stated.
